html:
The Podunk were a small Algonquian people of the Connecticut River valley, living along the Podunk River in today's East Hartford and South Windsor, Connecticut. They farmed maize and fished the river's spring runs of shad and salmon, and at times paid tribute to the more powerful Pequot.

English settlers founded Windsor and Hartford beside them in the 1630s, partly invited by river sachems looking for allies against the Pequot. After the Pequot War of 1636 to 1638 the Podunk sold most of their land, and some joined Metacom in King Philip's War in 1675 and did not return. Their neighbours included the Tunxis and the Wangunk. The name Podunk lives on in American English as a joke name for a small, out-of-the-way town.
